Consider fine-slicing (oscillation ≤ 0.5°), flash-annealing, or trying a different cryoprotectant. Verify the oscillation range is smaller than the mosaicity.

answer.title: Elevated correction factor χ² = 4.8
answer.body: The chi-squared for correction factors is somewhat elevated (ideal ≈ 1.0). This may indicate moderate absorption effects, crystal decay, or slight model inadequacy. Usually not critical, but if data quality is worse than expected, investigate absorption or decay.

answer.title: Wilson second moment ⟨I²⟩/2⟨I⟩² = 0.686 — possible twinning
answer.body: The average second moment of the Wilson distribution is well below the theoretical value of 1.0 for untwinned acentric data (a perfect twin gives 0.5). This strongly suggests merohedral or pseudo-merohedral twinning. Run CTRUNCATE (via the AIMLESS pipeline) for the L-test and H-test to confirm. If twinned, structure solution requires twin-aware refinement in REFMAC5 or phenix.refine.

answer.title: High σ(spindle) = 2.782°
answer.body: The standard deviation of spindle (rotation) positions is above 0.5°. This suggests problems with the rotation axis calibration, goniometer, or oscillation range. Try increasing MAXIMUM_ERROR_OF_SPINDLE_POSITION= (e.g. to 4.0), or check that the oscillation range in the header is correct.

answer.title: Half-integer cluster indices detected (axis 3, axis 1, axis 2)

answer.body: Completeness below 80% may compromise downstream structure solution and refinement. Common causes: insufficient rotation range for the crystal symmetry, detector geometry issues blocking reflections, or overly aggressive resolution cutoff. For molecular replacement, aim for > 90% completeness; for anomalous phasing, > 95%.

answer.title: High correction factor χ² = 6.7
answer.body: The chi-squared goodness-of-fit for the correction factors (decay, absorption, modulation) is very high. This means the empirical corrections are struggling to model systematic errors in the data. Common causes: crystal decay (radiation damage), strong absorption from the mount or crystal, or anisotropic absorption from a non-spherical crystal. Try: adjust CORRECTIONS= (e.g. remove MODULATION), or check if the crystal mount is contributing scatter.

answer.title: High mosaicity = 2.000°
answer.body: Mosaicity above 1° causes reflection overlap and degrades data quality. Common causes: cryo-cooling stress, physical crystal damage, or inherent disorder. Consider fine-slicing (oscillation ≤ 0.5°), flash-annealing, or trying a different cryoprotectant. Verify the oscillation range is smaller than the mosaicity.

answer.title: High R-factor at low resolution (45.7% in first shell)
answer.body: Elevated R-factors in the lowest-resolution shell (where signal should be strongest) typically indicate a fundamental problem rather than ice rings. Check: is the indexing correct? Is the beam center accurate? Is the space group correct? A wrong indexing solution often manifests as high R at low resolution with acceptable R at high resolution.

answer.title: Outer shell: CC½=6.9%, I/σ=-0.1 — no useful signal
answer.body: The outermost resolution shell has negligible signal. This is normal if the resolution cutoff was set conservatively, but if you see many such shells, consider reducing the resolution limit in XDS.INP (INCLUDE_RESOLUTION_RANGE=) to speed up processing and reduce noise in the merged data.

answer.title: Very low indexing rate (17.2%)
answer.body: Fewer than 30% of spots were indexed. Common causes: wrong beam center (ORGX/ORGY), ice rings contributing non-Bragg spots, multiple crystals, or incorrect DETECTOR_DISTANCE. Try: verify beam center visually, add EXCLUDE_RESOLUTION_RANGE= for ice rings, increase MINIMUM_NUMBER_OF_PIXELS_IN_A_SPOT=, or use the Auto-Indexing tool below.

answer.title: High σ(spot) = 3.00 px
answer.body: The standard deviation between observed and predicted spot positions is above 3 pixels. This can happen with split reflections, high mosaicity, or poorly described detector geometry. Try increasing MAXIMUM_ERROR_OF_SPOT_POSITION= (e.g. to 6.0). If the crystal diffracts well but spots are split, check for multiple lattices or twinning.

answer.title: High σ(spindle) = 2.000°
answer.body: The standard deviation of spindle (rotation) positions is above 0.5°. This suggests problems with the rotation axis calibration, goniometer, or oscillation range. Try increasing MAXIMUM_ERROR_OF_SPINDLE_POSITION= (e.g. to 4.0), or check that the oscillation range in the header is correct.

answer.title: ISa = 10.0 — elevated systematic errors
answer.body: ISa below 10 indicates significant systematic errors beyond counting statistics. Possible causes: beam instability, crystal splitting, ice contamination, detector calibration issues, or absorption from a large loop/mount. Good experimental setups typically achieve ISa ≥ 20 (Diederichs, 2010).

answer.title: High mosaicity = 1.500°
answer.body: Mosaicity above 1° causes reflection overlap and degrades data quality. Common causes: cryo-cooling stress, physical crystal damage, or inherent disorder. Consider fine-slicing (oscillation ≤ 0.5°), flash-annealing, or trying a different cryoprotectant. Verify the oscillation range is smaller than the mosaicity.

answer.title: High R-meas (33.4%) despite acceptable ISa (10.0)
answer.body: When ISa is reasonable but R-meas is elevated, the most common cause is wrong space group — XDS may have assigned too-high symmetry, forcing non-equivalent reflections to merge. Try: re-run CORRECT with SPACE_GROUP_NUMBER=0 to let XDS re-evaluate, or run POINTLESS for an independent space group determination. Also check whether the unit cell is correct — a misindexed cell axis produces the same symptom.

answer.title: Low indexing rate (43.1%)
answer.body: Less than 50% of spots were indexed. This may be acceptable if there are ice rings or a second lattice, but check that beam center and detector geometry are correct. Consider excluding ice ring resolution ranges or increasing MINIMUM_NUMBER_OF_PIXELS_IN_A_SPOT=.

answer.title: Very large beam center shift (33.4 px)
answer.body: IDXREF refined the beam center by 33.4 pixels from the header value (ORGX 1007.3 → 1033.9, ORGY 1437.0 → 1416.7). Shifts this large risk mis-indexing. Verify the beam center visually using the Frame Viewer with a low-angle image, then update ORGX/ORGY in the parameter editor and re-run COLSPOT + IDXREF.

answer.title: Half-integer cluster indices detected (axis 3, axis 1, axis 2)
answer.body: The difference vector table shows systematic half-integer indices along axis 3, axis 1, axis 2. This usually means the corresponding unit cell axis is doubled relative to what IDXREF found. Check the reduced cell parameters below the cluster table — if an axis is suspiciously short, try doubling it via UNIT_CELL_CONSTANTS= with SPACE_GROUP_NUMBER=1. Alternatively, use well-separated SPOT_RANGEs instead of one continuous range (XDSwiki).
